A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research framework, renamed from CoAR to DCoAR, with matching method equations, benchmarks and substantial retained results. All 15 pages of v1 and 19 pages of v2, including appendices, figures and tables, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original DreamBench and StyleDrop evaluations, subject-style generation results, loss and insertion-depth ablations, and qualitative experiments in its appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original personalization experiments and reports additional component ablations and qualitative analyses in the main text and supplementary material.

M1.justification: The specified frozen backbone, layerwise tokens, DPP and CASR objectives, and Identity Mask composition remain unchanged in the method section and Equations (5)-(11). However, v2's introduction newly describes latent-gradient penalties, perturbed-context alignment and cross-layer collapse prevention that these equations do not contain. The PDFs do not resolve whether these represent intended procedural changes or inaccurate exposition.

E1.justification: Both versions use DreamBench for subject personalization, StyleDrop for style personalization, and their combination for subject-style generation. The appendix retains the same eight-subject, six-style evaluation. Added ablations and revised examples stay within these existing tasks and domains.

E2.justification: v2 adds DreamBooth (Flux), Yo'Chameleon and UniCTokens to the DreamBench comparison in Table 1 and compares them qualitatively in Figure 12. Yo'Chameleon was only discussed in v1. These additions substantially expand comparison with concept-injection methods; the earlier baselines and the ZipLoRA/B-LoRA style comparison remain.

E3.justification: The original benchmark samples, metrics, backbone, training budgets and insertion settings are retained. New ablations introduce separate DPP-loss controls, Identity Mask on/off conditions, and text-only/image-only configurations across insertion depths. In the new Figure 11, each depth is paired with a different prompt, limiting isolation of the depth effect.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's incremental loss, insertion-depth and CASR-weight analyses, v2 adds LMCL plus CASR without DPP (Table 3), separate DPP-component ablations (Table 6), Identity Mask removal (Figure 9), and modality-by-depth analysis (Figure 11). These examine previously untested component contributions. The earlier qualitative loss ablation is relocated into the main text.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for its experimental results. v2's additional tables retain the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes the proposed method's style-alignment score from 0.594 to 0.605, overtaking ZipLoRA's 0.597. Table 3 revises LMCL+DPP DINO/CLIP-I from 0.6902/0.7919 to 0.7142/0.8019. New baseline and ablation results substantially expand the evidence, while the proposed method's main DreamBench scores are retained with reduced precision. v2's ablation prose reports CLIP-T 0.2977 where Table 3 still gives 0.2968.

T1.justification: The mathematical model and loss definitions in Equations (1)-(11), and the appendix LoRA parameter-count derivation in Equations (12)-(16), are retained. No new theorem, proof or formal derivation accompanies the revised conceptual explanations.

C1.justification: v1 centers its contribution on efficient concept injection into a frozen AR backbone. v2 redefines the central novelty as overcoming shallow-injection fidelity loss through deep reinforcement and bridging the gap to adaptation-based methods. Its abstract explicitly distinguishes superiority over injection methods from competitiveness with adaptation methods, while the introduction claims state-of-the-art unified AR personalization.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of the DPP components' fidelity/control tradeoff, modality-specific failures, and Identity Mask protection against concept contamination. It expands the existing depth-overfitting observation into an explicit limitations section and motivates adaptive insertion depth. New introductory mechanism explanations conflict with the unchanged loss definitions, and the retained claim of second-place DINO performance overlooks the newly added higher-scoring Flux baseline.

D1.justification: v1's explicit code-repository link is absent from v2, removing an access pointer without establishing whether repository availability changed. Hardware, hyperparameters, resolution, training steps and parameter-count assumptions remain documented. v2 additionally makes the published-source provenance of competing Table 1 scores explicit.

R1.justification: v2 reorganizes personalization research around adaptation-based and concept-injection paradigms, positioning DCoAR specifically against shallow injection in Yo'Chameleon and newly cited UniCTokens. It adds references including Prefix-Tuning and StyleAR, while removing separate SDXL and latent-diffusion references. The central relationship to prior work changes substantially beyond citation formatting.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, personalization-related-work discussion and conclusion are substantially rewritten around deep versus shallow injection. CoAR becomes DCoAR, the title and author list change, sections become numbered, the supplement gains a more detailed hierarchy, and references move after the supplementary material.

P2.justification: v2 substantially recomposes the presentation: Table 1 groups diffusion and unified AR methods and removes the training-stage column; new diagnostic displays are added; earlier galleries and the loss visualization are relocated or recomposed. For example, a subset of v1's appendix Figure 12 becomes main-text Figure 4. The supplement also changes from two-column to single-column layout.

improvement.justification: The added concept-injection baselines and targeted component ablations strengthen empirical assessment. However, v2 introduces regularization descriptions inconsistent with its unchanged equations, a Table 3/prose numerical disagreement, and a depth analysis that changes prompts across depths; it also removes the code link. These useful additions coexist with new problems in scientific coherence and reporting, preventing a confident judgment of net overall improvement.
